trans-unit.target: Type this card’s code into your basket when you check out. Whatever is left stays usable on a later order.
For the cases where no sale creates the card: a gesture after an incident, a card sold face to face, cards the shop already had. The code is drawn at random and shown once, on submit.
Print this page, then cut the card along the dotted line: the front first, the back after it.
Optional. The card is sent straight to them; leave it empty to get it yourself and pass it on.
Take up the habit of reading what the weekly check found, and of opening the orders behind it
Take a percentage or a fixed sum off an order, within the limits the code carries itself
Let every order leave with its invoice and the terms the customer has just accepted
Mint a card no sale created - a gesture after an incident, a card sold face to face, the cards the shop already had
Write an order for a deposit, a repair or an invoice, and hand its address to whoever settles it
Go from the orders owing a parcel to the e-mail telling each customer theirs is on its way
State what posting a parcel costs, zone by zone and weight tier by weight tier. As long as nothing is written, every delivery is free of charge.
Walk the whole checkout tunnel without charging a real customer
Reconcile a payment recorded here against its real entry at Stripe or another provider
Once the order is handled, mark the row rather than running the whole check again: it leaves the default view and comes back on its own if the problem reappears.

None of this raises anything of its own: an order charged and never delivered has no error page and no email to report itself. This screen is the only place it shows, and it only serves if it is opened.
A count does not say what to do: the unfolded list names the orders behind it, each with its link to open it in the back office. That is where the work starts.

The screen gathers everything the site checks on its own. Six of those rows are about your orders: a payment you were paid whose order never went out, an order delivered with no payment answering for it, an amount or a currency that does not match, an order delivered without its invoice number, lines that do not add up, a basket holding an article withdrawn from the catalogue.

They carry the "basket-integrity" kind and each says how many orders it found. Orders placed in test mode are left out: a shop rehearsing its checkout writes orders nobody settles or delivers, and every one of them would read here as a defect.
The six checks run on their own every week. This button runs them straight away, if the page is empty or if you have just fixed something.
What the customer types in their basket. It is dictated and retyped, so keep it short and free of anything read two ways.
Percentage or fixed amount. This choice is what the next field is read by, the two sharing one column.
How many orders may spend it at most, alongside the minimum an order has to reach and the two dates framing it - each one refused on its own, at the moment the order is frozen.
Its counter is raised by settled orders alone, and its Test mode column says which mode the shop was charging in the day it was written - a rehearsal code is never spendable for real.
The usual New button: unlike a gift card, a code holds no money and is written straight into the form.
Every code the shop wrote is listed there, with what it takes off and how often it has been spent.
Read as a percentage for the first kind, and in cents for the second: 10 is either a tenth of the order or ten cents off it.
The tile is no longer highlighted and now offers to turn it off: that is the only sign to read, the sending itself only showing on the next order.
Place a rehearsal order in test mode: its confirmation should arrive with the files ticked on that template. If none comes, the switch is on but nothing was ticked in the email builder.

The tile stays highlighted while the sending is off: handing the customer the terms they accepted as a file, rather than as a link to a page rewritten afterwards, is what the law calls a durable medium.

The shop's switches are here, as tiles. This one decides whether your order emails carry files at all; which files is ticked template by template in the email builder, which the "Tailor an e-mail" project walks through.
It is typed in the shop's own currency and becomes the card's whole balance, which its holder spends over as many orders as it takes.
It is shown once, in the message above the listing you land back on. No screen prints it again, so hand it over before leaving that page.
The code is drawn at random on submit, the same way a purchase draws one - nothing about it is typed.
Every card is listed there, sold or issued by hand: the ones written here are told apart by naming no order.
The Issue button, above the listing - and no New one: the balance is minted from the amount rather than typed, and never edited afterwards.
Left empty, the card never expires. Filled in, it stops being spendable that day, whatever balance is left on it.
It is typed in the shop's own currency and VAT included, as every price here is; the tax is taken out of it at the rate the payment-link-vat-rate setting holds.
The order is frozen there and then, and its short address appears above the form: send it by text message or by e-mail, and it is settled online like any other.
The confirmation goes there once the order is settled, and it is what attaches the order to their account should they open one.
What the customer reads on their order, on their invoice and in their confirmation e-mail: "Deposit for the flooring", "Bicycle repair".
A payment link is written from the orders listing, which is where the one it creates comes to sit.
The Payment link button, above the listing: there is no row to start from, the order being written by the form it opens.
A marked order leaves the ones awaiting shipping, so tomorrow's sheet holds only what is still owed. A counterpart is sent by the button beside it, on its own.
Paid is the only state a parcel leaves on: an order merely validated has not been settled, and nothing is posted for it.
Only an active zone is read at checkout. Save, then write the next zone the same way.

The health check screen reports what the grid does not say: no zone at all, no default zone or several of them, a zone without a boundless tier. Read it once the grid is written rather than on a month of orders.
The countries posted at this tariff. Leave the list empty for the default zone, the one a country named nowhere else falls into - write that one too, or such an order is delivered free of charge.
The name is yours alone: "France", "European Union", "Rest of the world". The customer never reads it.
A zone groups the countries you post at one tariff, and carries its weight tiers with it.
The screen lists the zones already written. An empty list is a shop posting everything free of charge.
One price per weight tier, the parcel charged at the first tier it fits in. End with a tier left without a ceiling, otherwise a heavier parcel than any of them is posted free of charge.
One sheet for the whole round, opened in another tab: it gathers the orders awaiting shipping that carry an address, and says so when there are none.
Every order is listed there, whatever its state - which is more than a shipping round needs.
On the row of the order just packed. It only shows on a paid order carrying something to post and not yet marked, and the click both records the shipping and e-mails the customer.
The basket shows its test-payment banner; run a full payment to check the order does turn into paid.
The same shortcut, its label now changed, switches the shop back to the real keys.
The test payment stays among the payments, told apart by an order carrying no invoice at all: a rehearsal never enters the invoice sequence.
The shop switches to the active provider's test keys; nobody is charged while it stays on.
The test-payments shortcut sits there, next to the maintenance one.
The Basket column leads back to the baskets screen, carrying the address, the content and the order's status.
The originating basket, the currency and the transaction id are gathered there.
Every payment is listed there with its provider, amount and status.
The Transaction icon opens it on Stripe's dashboard, once an id has been recorded. Revolut publishes no stable address for an order, so the icon is absent there and only the id is shown.
The "Payment system" setting is empty or names a provider no bundle registers: no basket can be paid.
The live %gateway% keys are not filled in, or cannot be read: validating a basket fails.
Test payments are enabled and the %gateway% test keys are not filled in, or cannot be read: validating a basket fails.
Charge for what the catalogue does not sell: a deposit, a repair, an invoice. The order is written frozen, and its link is settled online like any other.
"Shop email (blind copy)" is empty: no copy of the order confirmations and download links is kept. Fill in an address to keep a record of them.
